messages:
Priya: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands on credits/burst behavior. Two questions: 1) Do promo/top-up credits change rate limits? 2) How do we handle large embedding spikes from trial orgs?

Leo: TL;DR: credits are currency only, they don't increase throughput limits. Promo credits reduce invoice balance but rate limiting is independent.

Carmen: For trials: we give a small shared burst pool for first 48h to reduce signup friction. After that the key is subject to normal per-key QPS and concurrent request limits.

Priya: Can we show a tiny example math so PMs can explain billing?

Leo: Example: 1k-token embed * 10k items = 10M tokens. At $0.0003/token that's $3,000. A $1k promo credit covers part; the remainder is billed. Rate limits can still block parallel submission and cause failures.

Nikhil: Ops note: limits enforced are (1) per-key QPS, (2) per-route concurrent, (3) token-rate smoothing. We allow micro-bursts for a few seconds, then enforce the average. Sustained high throughput should use Dedicated commit.

Priya: Where is credit balance visible?

ops-bot: Console -> Billing -> Credits shows current balance. API header: X-Credit-Balance. See internal doc: /handbook/billing/credits.md

Carmen: Fallbacks: if we serve a cheaper model during regional pressure, billing is for the model actually served. We emit X-Model-Served and X-Fallback-Reason so customers can reconcile.

Priya: Support needs a canned response for "I got 429 but I have credits"

Leo: Draft: "A 429 means your request rate exceeded allowed throughput. Credits pay for tokens but do not raise rate caps. Check X-RateLimit-* headers. For sustained higher RPS request Dedicated or contact sales for a review"

Carmen: I'll add that to canned replies and update the FAQ.

Priya: Thanks, team. Closing thread. :thumbsup:
